title: Sessionless SDK compatibility & migration examples for streaming tool invocations and structured outputs
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background:
We are shipping new server-side streaming + tool/function-calling features that emit incremental structured outputs (framed JSON events) across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. Existing customers and older SDKs expect synchronous, session-bound tool calls and blocking generator patterns. This ticket delivers a compatibility layer and concrete migration examples (sessionless invocation pattern) so older clients can adopt streaming outputs and tool-calls without breaking behavior.

Scope and goals:
- Define a sessionless invocation envelope that supports both: progressive token/event streaming and out-of-band tool/function invocation events (start, progress, result, error).
- Implement SDK helper shims in TS/Python/Go that map streaming envelopes into blocking iterators/promises and backwards-compatible callback APIs.
- Provide recipe-level migration guides and 3 runnable examples (TS chat + tool, Python embedder + structured output, Go microservice using streaming + tool results).
- Add conformance tests and a compatibility e2e in examples repo.
- Address security review around tool-identity headers and cross-origin stream routing.

Non-goals:
- Full refactor of existing SDK internals; shims should be additive and lightweight.
acceptance_criteria: Define a simple sessionless event envelope and publish spec to Confluence
Three SDK helper shims (TS/Python/Go) with identical semantic surface published in examples repo
Migration guide with before/after snippets for each language and one end-to-end CI job that verifies behavior for both old synchronous and new streaming clients
Security review completed and any required header/auth changes documented
Performance regression <3% on standard token throughput for shimmed paths (bench report attached)
comments: 2026-03-01 - Liam Chen: Initial ticket created after spike showing divergence between blocking client expectations and new streaming events. Referenced runtime design notes (Confluence).
2026-03-03 - Aisha Raman: Scoped to be shim-only to accelerate adoption; flagged security review. Added labels and estimate 5 pts.
2026-03-05 - Eng-Review (Pedro Alvarez): Reviewed envelope draft; recommended explicit 'event_type' field and stable 'session_id' optional header to simplify routing for legacy proxies.

2026-03-06 - Design (Maya Patel): Provided UX examples for the TypeScript Promise wrapper and Python generator docstrings. Suggests example showing graceful fallback to smaller model for tool execution timeouts.

2026-03-08 - Aisha Raman: Draft shims implemented for TS and Python (internal branch). Running integration tests against runtime staging cluster; initial failures on partial tool-result ordering (race identified).

2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Opened PRs: GH-Redwood/sdk-examples#482 (TS shim + chat-tool sample), GH-Redwood/sdk-examples#485 (Python generator shim + embedder sample). Added conformance test plan in examples repo.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: lightweight shim vs full SDK rewrite. We chose shim to minimize customer churn and allow gradual adoption of streaming-first APIs. Edge case: proxy servers that buffer streaming responses will break progressive delivery; note added to migration doc. Will track adoption metrics via console usage dashboard after release.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize envelope spec and security headers; 2) Implement TS helper (Promise + progressive event callback) and publish example; 3) Implement Python generator shim and publish example; 4) Implement Go compatibility helper (channel-based iterator) and publish example; 5) Add e2e conformance tests and CI; 6) Security review and docs; 7) Announce migration guide and monitor adoption.
risks: Proxies/balancers that buffer will negate streaming benefits; some customers may prefer full-session APIs for long-running tool calls. Need coordination with Console team to add migration checklist and warning banners for buffered routes.
customer_notes: We will provide migration snippets in three languages and a compatibility mode toggle. Offer support session for enterprise customers migrating Dedicated/Private deployments.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope parsing, integration tests exercising tool start/complete/error events ordering, and e2e running against staging runtime with sample tools (echo, external-http-caller). CI to run on PRs. Performance benchmark comparison against baseline without shim.
